test_doctrine.principle: Tests target substrate seam boundaries — where data crosses from one stage to the next in the architecture pipeline. Every seam must have a test that would fail if the seam leaks (content-light, format fidelity, schema governance, redaction).

classification_legend.contract: adapter satisfies its Port interface contract
classification_legend.e2e: full pipeline from artifact to projection
classification_legend.real-artifact: uses real JSON/JSONL/CSV fixtures from tests/fixtures/
classification_legend.substrate: verifies specific database-adjacent tool behavior (Parquet, Arrow, COPY, Zstandard)

test_suites.title: Zstandard Expansion Roundtrip and Redaction Tests
test_suites.description: Verify Zstandard compression/decompression roundtrip preserves content. Verify zstd-compressed bundles fail redaction scan if decompressed content leaks forbidden material. Verify zstd compression ratio meets or exceeds gzip baseline.
test_cases: JSONL → zstd compress → zstd decompress → JSONL roundtrip preserves all fields
zstd compressed bundle passes content-light redaction scan on decompress
zstd compressed bundle FAILS redaction scan if forbidden content exists in decompressed output
zstd compression ratio >= gzip for representative session JSONL
zstd decompression failure returns structured error, not silent corruption
zstd-empty input produces valid empty archive
zstd-truncated input detected as corrupt, not silently decompressed

test_suites.title: Pydantic Expansion Contract Tests
test_suites.description: Verify Pydantic model_validate/model_dump_json replaces stdlib json at module boundaries. Verify type safety and extra='forbid' enforcement.
test_cases: Pydantic model_validate rejects extra fields beyond schema
Pydantic model_dump_json output is valid canonical JSON
Pydantic model roundtrip (dump → load → dump) produces identical SHA256
Pydantic model rejects forbidden content patterns (CHECK constraint equivalent)
stdlib json.loads bypass produces same result as Pydantic model_validate for known-valid input

test_suites.title: Arrow In-Memory Interchange Tests
test_suites.description: Verify Arrow table → dict roundtrip preserves schema-governed fields. Verify Arrow table ↔ Pydantic model roundtrip. Verify Arrow-backed projections contain no raw content.
test_cases: JSONL → Arrow → JSONL roundtrip preserves all schema-governed fields
Arrow table → dict projection payload is bit-identical to dict-only projection payload
Arrow schema derived from Pydantic model matches expected column types
Arrow table never contains raw content fields

test_suites.title: Parquet Derived Snapshot Doctrine Tests
test_suites.description: Verify Parquet snapshots never become canonical event truth. Verify JSONL → Parquet → DuckDB query parity. Verify Parquet read-back yields same content-light results as JSONL read.
test_cases: JSONL → Parquet → DuckDB query parity: same counts, same aggregates
Parquet snapshots classified as derived, not canonical, in artifact_registry
Parquet read via DuckDB produces same content-light projection as JSONL read
Parquet snapshot can be fully rebuilt from canonical JSONL (replay test)
Corrupted Parquet snapshot is detected and triggers rebuild from JSONL

test_suites.title: Postgres COPY Ingestion and Export Tests
test_suites.description: Verify COPY FROM with staging table validates constraints. Verify COPY TO produces valid JSONL that matches canonical artifacts. Verify COPY rejects invalid schema rows in staging.
test_cases: COPY FROM to staging table: valid rows promoted, invalid rows rejected with structured error
COPY FROM rejects rows that fail CHECK constraints (schema_version format, artifact_sha256 format)
COPY FROM rejects rows with forbidden content keys (token, secret, raw_prompt)
COPY TO export produces valid JSONL matching canonical artifact row count
COPY TO → COPY FROM roundtrip preserves all generated column values
COPY with empty input produces zero rows (no error)
COPY with truncated JSONL input detects incomplete final row

test_suites.title: No Raw Content Across Substrate Seams
test_suites.description: Verify that no substrate tool (Arrow, Parquet, Zstandard, COPY, DuckDB) can be used to bypass content-light enforcement or introduce raw content into any stage of the pipeline.
test_cases: Arrow table construction rejects forbidden fields
Parquet generation from raw JSONL rejects forbidden content
Zstandard decompressed bundle passes content-light scan
Postgres COPY FROM staging rejects forbidden content keys
DuckDB query output contains only envelope-level fields (no raw payloads)
Cockpit projection generated from Arrow/Parquet contains no raw private content
Static docs projection scan catches absolute paths/tokens/source snippets
Procurement pack generation uses content-light derived summaries only

test_suites.title: Substrate Performance Regression Tests
test_suites.description: Track performance of key substrate operations against baseline. Alert on regression >20%.
test_cases: JSONL ingestion throughput (rows/sec) does not regress >20% from baseline
DuckDB projection compute time per widget does not regress >20% from baseline
Static docs render time does not regress >20% from baseline per 100 pages
Parquet compaction throughput (rows/sec) within 2x of JSONL read time

test_suites.title: pgvector Sensitive Derived Data Safety Tests
test_suites.phase: Phase 6 (only if pgvector promoted from park)
test_suites.description: Verify embeddings never store raw private repo text. Verify embedding records are classified as sensitive derived data. Verify local-only boundary enforcement.
test_cases: Embedding record contains only content_sha256 + vector, never raw text
Embedding record classified as sensitive derived data in audit trail
Local-only embeddings cannot be exported to product telemetry
pgvector unavailable → semantic search returns empty, not error
